title: Earliest surviving silk fabric
summary: The earliest surviving silk fabric, wrapped around a child's body at a Yangshao culture site near Xingyang, dates to about 3630 BCE. Traces of silk protein at Jiahu are far older.
why: Silk later drove trade routes across Eurasia.

notes.problem: Overclaim: summary says 'earliest evidence of silk garments'; cited timeline only says 'Silk garments (sericulture) in China' (3630 BC). Silk article: earliest silk evidence is Jiahu fibroin ~8,500 years ago; 3630 BC is the 'earliest surviving example of silk fabric' at Qingtaicun.
